Q: Merging two sorted arrays into a third one can be done in O(n)? A:

(The sizes of the sorted input arrays are m and n.)
Worst-case, you need m + n - 1 comparisons to merge them. O(m+n).
Best-case, IF the ranges don't overlap at all, the simplest merge algorithm will perform either m comparisons or n comparisons. (m if the first list comes first; n if the second list comes first.) Making O(max?(m,n)).
Looking ahead can let it skip many unnecessary comparisons, but it risks adding wasted comparisons.
Looking ahead once, at the beginning, in the above example with no overlap, would "reduce" the best-case comparisons from max?(m,n) to min(m,n) + log2(m) - 1, or O(min(m,n).)
Looking ahead while merging could avoid many comparisons IF the result isn't tightly interleaved (it receives some long "runs" from either input array). Looking ahead is guesswork, so the better guessing algorithm will be heuristic and a little adaptive. When merging random data, looking ahead by 1 costs a wasted comparison about as often as it saves a comparison. But with non-random data, the net savings can be larger. If long runs exist, adaptively looking ahead by a larger distances could save a lot of comparisons. You could do way better than O(m+n), depending on your skill at making the guessing algorithm and its match to the distributions of the actual nonrandom data. You'll need an algorithm for the forward guess (twice as far ahead as last time?) and one for the fallback guesses after a wrong guess (half as far ahead as the last guess?).
Another way to describe this approach is: After picking a side, see how many more in a row you can take from that side without checking them all.

Q: heroku zerigo dns - www.xxx.in working but xxx.in sometimes giving application error (sometimes working) A:

This setup should work on three conditions:

  1. Your root DNS has A records pointing to Heroku's designated routing IPs
  2. You have added your naked domain to your application (heroku domains:add example.com)
  3. Your application supports your naked domain

Check all these points, a problem in each one can cause things not to work.

If you are redirecting on the DNS/host provider level from the naked domain to www. then none of this is needed, and you have a configuration problem with your host which is out of scope for this question.

Q: Weblogic Ant JWSC task to generate a webservice war file A:

I'm betting that in your deployment target (Which isn't posted here) is trying to 'clean' up the deployment directory, and is failing when it can't find the file called /var/tmp/_927vxb/web.xml

3 suggestions:

  1. Run touch /var/tmp/_927vxb/web.xml from the command line and try to run the build/deployment again. This will create an empty file that will at least let you get past the file not found on delete error. This is not a long term solution, but rather an attempt to expose the real issue.

  2. Look at line 231 in your /wls_domains/CIT/cruisecontrol-bin-2.8.3/util/Ivy/build.xml file. Perhaps there is a delete ant task that is failing on error. If this is the case, add `failonerror="false" to the ant task that is causing the issue.

  3. Post more of your build file here. Being able to align the line numbers in the file with the error will help in decoding the issue.

Q: Does Querying multiple EFCore DbSets in a single LINQ call still result in a single SQL Query that is executed on the database? A:

Trying this out for yourself is the best approach, in my opinion. If you have a use case for this already, go ahead and write the EF LINQ query. Next, turn on Entity Framework SQL logging, and start your application in a debug session in Visual Studio. Be sure you have "Debug" or "Information" log messages enabled in your main logger in the application.

Upon starting your application, a console window should open up which will display those log messages. The SQL statements should appear in the console window as you execute a use case.
